overview: Mapletree Industrial Trust (MIT) is a Singapore-listed REIT that owns a S$8.3 billion portfolio of 136 industrial and data centre properties as at 31 March 2026, comprising 79 properties in Singapore, 55 in North America (42 wholly owned plus a 50% joint-venture interest in 13 data centres held via Mapletree Rosewood Data Centre Trust) and two in Japan. The trust earns rental income from four reportable segments -- Data Centres (Asia), Data Centres (North America), Hi-Tech Buildings and Business Space, and General Industrial Buildings -- and is externally managed by Mapletree Industrial Trust Management Ltd., a wholly-owned subsidiary of its sponsor, Mapletree Investments Pte Ltd. MIT reports in SGD on a fiscal year ending 31 March.

business_model.summary: MIT generates recurring rental income (plus service charges and car park/other operating income) from long-leased industrial and data centre real estate, distributing at least 90% of taxable income to unitholders as required of a Singapore REIT. Growth comes from a mix of organic rental reversions/AEIs on the stable Singapore base, income from US/Japan data centres, and recycling capital through acquisitions and divestments (e.g. the FY25/26 S$535.3m Singapore Portfolio Divestment and Osaka Data Centre fit-out completion). Revenue is split roughly: North America data centres ~34% of FY25/26 gross revenue (S$227.8m of S$673.0m), General Industrial Buildings (flatted factories, stack-up/ramp-up, light industrial) ~34% (S$226.5m), Hi-Tech Buildings and Business Space ~25% (S$168.3m), and Asia (Japan) data centres ~7.5% (S$50.5m).

revenue_streams.name: General Industrial Buildings (Singapore - flatted factories, stack-up/ramp-up, light industrial)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - tenants span technology/data centre operators (hyperscale, colocation and enterprise users), light manufacturing, electronics, logistics and business park occupiers; master lease and build-to-suit structures with large anchor tenants are common in North America
business_model.geographic_mix: Assets under management by geography (31 Mar 2026): North America 46.5%, Singapore 46.3%, Japan 7.2%. By asset type: Data Centres 57.3% of AUM (North America 46.5%, Japan 7.2%, Singapore 3.6%), with the balance in Hi-Tech Buildings/Business Space and General Industrial Buildings

main_competitors: Mapletree Logistics Trust (sister trust, different asset class)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest Singapore-listed industrial/data centre REITs by AUM (S$8.3bn), with the highest data centre weighting (~57% of AUM) among diversified Singapore industrial REITs; competes with pure-play Keppel DC REIT for data centre capital and tenants, and with CLAR/ESR-REIT for conventional Singapore industrial space

moat_factors.description: Mapletree Investments (a major global real estate developer/manager with ~S$80bn+ AUM) provides right-of-first-refusal pipeline access, development expertise (e.g. Osaka Data Centre, Tokyo acquisition) and co-investment via joint ventures (MRODCT North American data centre JV)
136 properties across Singapore, North America and Japan reduce single-tenant/sector concentration, though data centre weighting concentrates cyclicality in one asset class

moat_factors.factor: Long leasehold/freehold US data centre assets with embedded tenants
moat_factors.description: Many North American data centres are freehold with long-term leases to hyperscale/enterprise users, though enterprise-configured assets outside primary markets face renewal risk

moat_factors.factor: Credit ratings and access to capital
moat_factors.description: Fitch BBB+ (Stable) and new AA- (Stable) ratings from JCR/R&I support access to diversified funding (bank loans, MTNs, perpetual securities) at competitive cost (3.1% average FY25/26)

moat_factors.factor: Singapore government land scarcity / planning barriers
moat_factors.description: Limited new industrial land supply in Singapore supports pricing power and occupancy for the Singapore portfolio, which achieved ~7% positive rental reversions in FY25/26

weaknesses: High and rising exposure to US data centres (46.5% of AUM) with enterprise-tenant configurations that are less optimised for hyperscale/colocation demand, driving non-renewals
External management structure creates fee-based incentive misalignment versus an internally managed REIT
No pricing power over broad macro/interest-rate cycle; distributions are directly exposed to swap repricing
Currency mismatch - USD and JPY income translated into SGD reporting currency creates FX volatility and NAV erosion (NAV/unit fell 4.7% YoY in FY25/26 partly on USD/JPY depreciation)
Smaller/pure-play data centre peers (e.g. Keppel DC REIT) can be viewed by investors as cleaner proxies for the AI/data centre theme

growth_drivers: AI/hyperscale and cloud demand driving data centre absorption - North America primary market vacancy at a record low 1.4% (end-2025) per CBRE, with capacity up 36% YoY to 9.4GW
Rebalancing the North American data centre portfolio towards cloud/hyperscale and colocation providers, away from enterprise tenants, to capture higher-quality, longer-term demand

Growth in Japan data centre market - Osaka upgraded to "Established Market" status (Cushman & Wakefield), full income contribution from completed Osaka Data Centre fit-out, and Tokyo mixed-use property acquired Oct 2024
Disciplined capital recycling - targeting a further S$500m-S$600m of North American divestments to fund value-accretive acquisitions in data centres across Asia Pacific and Europe
Asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs) and redevelopment of the Singapore portfolio to improve competitiveness and unlock density/value
Positive rental reversions across all Singapore property segments (~7.0% weighted average in FY25/26) supporting organic income growth
Continued sponsor pipeline access to Mapletree's global real estate development and data centre platform

business.description: ~5.1% of North American leases by gross rental income are due for expiry in FY26/27, of which ~4.7% already confirmed as non-renewals, concentrated in enterprise-tenant assets outside primary data centre markets; North American occupancy fell to 87.4% in FY25/26 from 89.3%

business.risk: Geographic/asset class concentration in data centres
business.description: Data centres are 57.3% of AUM (46.5% in North America alone); a downturn or oversupply in hyperscale/cloud demand would disproportionately affect MIT versus more diversified industrial REIT peers

Active divestment/acquisition recycling (S$550.6m divested FY25/26, further S$500-600m targeted) creates near-term income gaps and execution risk around redeployment into accretive Asia Pacific/Europe data centre assets

financial.description: About S$600 million of interest rate hedges expire in FY26/27 and are expected to reprice at higher rates than when contracted, exerting downward pressure on distributions; 88.6% of total borrowings hedged to fixed as at 31 Mar 2026
Significant USD- and JPY-denominated income and asset values are translated into SGD; USD/JPY depreciation reduced FY25/26 gross revenue, NPI and NAV per unit (down 4.7% YoY to S$1.63)

Aggregate leverage was 34.0% as at 31 Mar 2026 but management expects it to rise to ~37.5% after redeploying new perpetual securities proceeds to redeem the Series 002 perpetual securities; MIT reported a net current liabilities position due to borrowings maturing within a year
New S$300m Series 006 perpetual securities issued at 3.25% (replacing 3.15% Series 002), increasing the cost of hybrid capital embedded ahead of distributions to unitholders

regulatory.description: MIT's tax-transparency treatment depends on maintaining Singapore REIT distribution requirements (≥90% of taxable income); changes to MAS/IRAS REIT rules could affect distribution economics

Power procurement constraints, grid dependency and energy/utility cost inflation in data centre markets (partly mitigated by tenant cost pass-through and Singapore power contracts through Dec 2026 for ~20% of the portfolio)

macro.risk: Global growth slowdown and geopolitical tensions
macro.description: IMF projects global growth moderating to 3.1% in 2026 from 3.4% in 2025, with the Middle East conflict escalation in early 2026 raising energy price volatility and tightening financial conditions

Singapore manufacturing/trade sector growth is sensitive to global electronics demand; North American data centre vacancy and rents are sensitive to hyperscale capex cycles and AI investment sentiment

FY25/26 portfolio valuation fell to S$7,286.3m (MIT Group investment properties) partly due to valuers applying less favourable sales-comparison assumptions to North American properties with vacancy/near-term lease expiry risk

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Favorable long-term structural demand for data centres driven by AI training/inference, cloud and hyperscale growth, but near-term headwinds from enterprise-tenant lease attrition in secondary US markets; Singapore industrial property benefiting from land scarcity and resilient manufacturing/trade sector; Japan data centre market (Tokyo, Osaka) in rapid expansion
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - rental income is largely contracted and recurring (WALE 6.3 years North America, 13.7 years Japan), but data centre segment is exposed to hyperscale capex cycles, enterprise tenant churn, and valuation marks tied to discount/capitalisation rate movements
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - REIT structure with S$2.35bn total borrowings (34.0% aggregate leverage); average borrowing cost 3.1%, interest coverage 4.0x; ~S$600m of interest rate swaps reprice in FY26/27, directly affecting DPU
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Material - USD (North America, ~46.5% of AUM) and JPY (Japan, ~7.2% of AUM) income and asset values translate into SGD reporting currency; ~92.5% of amount available for distribution in the next 12 months is hedged into or derived in SGD to stabilise distributions
key_input_costs: Construction/fit-out costs for AEIs and redevelopment

recent_developments.event: FY25/26 full-year results: gross revenue down 5.5% YoY to S$673.0m, NPI down 5.9% to S$500.4m, DPU down 6.3% YoY to 12.71 cents; aggregate leverage improved to 34.0% from 40.1% following divestment proceeds

Issued S$300 million of 3.25% fixed-rate perpetual securities (Series 006) ahead of the May 2026 redemption of the 3.15% Series 002 perpetual securities; broadened credit ratings with new AA- (Stable) ratings from JCR and R&I alongside existing Fitch BBB+ (Stable)
JPMorgan downgraded MIT to Underweight with a S$1.90 price target (from S$2.50), citing expected vacancies in US and Singapore data centres and a forecast DPU decline of ~4% per year
Completed the Singapore Portfolio Divestment (The Strategy, The Synergy, Woodlands Central Cluster) for S$535.3 million, a 22.1% premium to original cost and 2.6% premium to market valuation

Completed the final phase of fitting-out works at the Osaka Data Centre (JPY5.2bn, ~10% of purchase consideration) and divested the Georgia Data Centre (2775 Northwoods Parkway) for US$11.8 million, an 18.6% premium to its independent valuation

North American portfolio occupancy declined to 87.4% (from 89.3%) on non-renewal of enterprise-tenant leases; management targeting re-leasing to cloud/hyperscale and colocation tenants and continuing selective North American divestments of S$500m-S$600m
Board appointment of Ms Soo Yar Ping as Independent Non-Executive Director; Mr Guy Daniel Harvey-Samuel to step down from the Board in July 2026

Analyst consensus mixed-to-cautious: average one-year price targets clustering around S$2.00-S$2.05 (Investing.com, Fintel, Simply Wall St), with Goldman Sachs at Neutral/Hold (S$2.12 target) and JPMorgan at Underweight, reflecting concerns over US data centre vacancy and DPU trajectory

guidance.as_of: FY25/26 Annual Results (28 May 2026) / Q4 FY25/26 Results Announcement

items.period: FY26/27 and beyond (multi-year selective divestment programme)
items.notes: Recycling capital out of North American data centres with elevated vacancy/non-renewal risk into Asia Pacific and Europe data centre opportunities; S$550.6m already completed in FY25/26

Expected increase following debt drawdown and redeployment of new perpetual securities proceeds to redeem the Series 002 Perpetual Securities in May 2026; still within MAS regulatory leverage limit (50%) and provides headroom for acquisitions

items.metric: North American data centre lease expiries
items.target: ~5.1% of North American leases by gross rental income expiring in FY26/27, ~4.7% already confirmed non-renewals
items.notes: San Diego asset flagged as the largest single North American expiry; management actively engaging tenants ahead of expiry and evaluating selective divestment

items.target: ~S$600 million of interest rate hedges due for expiry
items.notes: Replacement hedges expected to be contracted at higher rates than the expiring (lower-rate) swaps, exerting downward pressure on distributions
MIT does not issue formal revenue/DPU guidance; management instead provides qualitative commentary on competitive conditions and known near-term factors each quarter

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Ler Lily and Chairman Cheah Kim Teck highlighted a strategy of 'Shaping Balance - Building Strength', emphasizing portfolio rebalancing away from enterprise-tenant North American data centres toward cloud/hyperscale and colocation providers, continued disciplined divestment/acquisition recycling into Asia Pacific and Europe data centres, and prudent capital management amid a more fragile global macro backdrop following the early-2026 Middle East conflict escalation. Management flagged confirmed North American non-renewals and swap repricing as the key known near-term (FY26/27) headwinds to business performance, while noting ~92.5% of distributable income over the next 12 months is SGD-hedged or SGD-derived to protect distribution stability.

bull_case: Direct exposure to structural AI/hyperscale and cloud data centre demand, with North American primary market vacancy at a record-low 1.4% and strong secular growth in Japan's Tokyo/Osaka data centre markets
Strong sponsor (Mapletree Investments) provides a global development and acquisition pipeline, demonstrated by the successful Osaka Data Centre build and Tokyo acquisition

Disciplined capital recycling - divesting lower-quality/at-risk North American assets at premiums to valuation (18.6% premium on Georgia, 22.1% premium on Singapore Portfolio Divestment) and redeploying into higher-quality data centre markets
Improved balance sheet flexibility - aggregate leverage reduced to 34.0%, average borrowing cost steady at 3.1%, and newly obtained AA- credit ratings broaden funding access

Resilient Singapore and Japan portfolios (92.9% and 100% occupancy respectively, positive ~7% rental reversions in Singapore) partially offsetting North American softness, with ~92.5% of distributable income SGD-hedged for income stability
bear_case: North American data centre portfolio concentration (46.5% of AUM) is exposed to enterprise-tenant non-renewals, with occupancy falling to 87.4% and ~4.7% of FY26/27 leases already confirmed as non-renewals

DPU has declined for multiple consecutive periods (down 6.3% YoY in FY25/26, down 8.0% in 4Q alone) and JPMorgan forecasts further ~4% annual DPU declines amid continued US/Singapore data centre vacancy risk
Rising cost of debt and hedges - ~S$600m of interest rate swaps reprice higher in FY26/27, and aggregate leverage is expected to rise to ~37.5%, both pressuring distributable income

FX headwinds from USD and JPY depreciation against SGD have reduced reported gross revenue, NPI and NAV per unit (down 4.7% YoY to S$1.63), and will persist as long as a large data centre book sits offshore

Mixed-to-cautious analyst sentiment (JPMorgan Underweight, Goldman Sachs Neutral/Hold) reflects skepticism about near-term execution of the North America-to-Asia Pacific/Europe portfolio rebalancing strategy
